description:
Corrects a systematic error across all 7 approved '-600' de-restriction signs. Every one carried the same boilerplate testHint claiming a DIAGONAL STRIPE ends a restriction. SARTSM Vol 1 Ch 2 §2.9 is explicit that de-restriction is a RED CROSS superimposed on the original sign, and that the diagonal slash is the prohibition marker. All 7 were live to learners. Surfaced 2026-08-03 by a question-drafting agent that rejected R202-600 as a candidate because its stored hint contradicted the manual — writing questions forces you to state precisely what a sign means, which is why the drafting pass keeps finding content defects.

OPEN, NOT FIXED HERE: whether our -600 ARTWORK shows a cross or a slash was not resolved. The SVGs carry red elements but the markup alone does not settle it, and guessing is how the original error got in. Needs a visual check against the chart — see docs/verification-worklist.md.

testHint.en: A red CROSS over a regulatory sign is what ends the rule it shows. A red diagonal slash is the opposite — it means prohibited. Do not read one for the other.

behaviour.en: No toll-route requirement applies beyond this point.

plainEnglish.en: This sign marks the END of the toll route. From here, you are leaving the toll-road section.

commonMistake.en: Thinking the toll route still applies past this sign — it does not; the rule has ended here.

formalMeaning.en: Regulatory sign R132-600: it cancels the toll route that applied on the road behind you.

ops.why: testHint read 'A regulatory sign with a diagonal stripe through it means the rule it shows has ENDED.' That inverts the marker. SARTSM Vol 1 Ch 2 §2.9 (resources/sartsm/V1C2.pdf): 'DE-RESTRICTION is achieved by displaying the original sign with a RED CROSS (R)600 superimposed on the face of the sign', and it adds that 'the use of the (R)600 element with PROHIBITION signs using a diagonal slash, is not recommended' — i.e. the diagonal slash is the PROHIBITION marker, not the end-of-restriction marker. Teaching a learner to read a prohibition slash as 'no longer applies' is a safety-relevant inversion. Identical boilerplate hint was present on all 7 of the -600 signs and all 7 were approved and live; corrected together.
